title: Data scaling Q(n): does the frozen family's accuracy scale with training rows comparably to a cost-matched dense trunk?

device._note: frozen sparse encode and the DINOv2-small trunk forward on the GPU ('cuda' = ROCm/HIP, HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, gfx1201); whitening and ridge on numpy CPU (M107 arithmetic).

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

sparse.layer0_dictionary: M108/M113 arm (a) exact: prefix of the seeded permutation of the shared 8192-whitened-patch pool - IDENTICAL to the dictionary M113 measured at 0.2153
sparse.head: closed_form_ridge_1.0 (M108's constant, unchanged)
sparse._note: M116 fits the BEST arm measured in M115, which was L=0 (the frozen single-stage 3072-dictionary arm); the depth arms lost. Data scaling of the depth stack is moot after M115 KS1 fired.

dense.protocol: t1: frozen DINOv2-small trunk (M109 DenseModel) + closed-form ridge head penalty 1.0, all train rows
dense._note: r42 is the best M107/M109 dense point at-or-below the sparse family's 254.6M per-image MACs (M107 gate rule): dense r42 0.19716 @ 215.6M. The Q(n) comparison is at matched per-image cost.

scaling.subsample_rule: the first n rows of the M107-shuffled train order (nested, deterministic, class-balanced by the shuffle); every ladder point is a subset of every later one
scaling.test_set: the full 34500-row shared test set, identical for every ladder point and both families
scaling._note: features are image functions, not n functions: the sparse codes and the dense trunk features are each computed ONCE over the full corpus (memmap on D:), then a ridge is fitted at each n from the first n rows. No re-encoding per ladder point.

gate.kill_switch_data_scaling: fired (fail) if the frozen family's accuracy gain across the n-ladder is less than half the dense trunk's gain: Delta_S = Q_S(n_max) - Q_S(n_min) >= 0.5 * Delta_T with Delta_T = Q_T(n_max) - Q_T(n_min). The family must improve with data at least half as fast as the cost-matched dense trunk, measured on the same nested ladder and the same full test set. Reported: per-n table, the gap Q_T(n) - Q_S(n) at each n (must not diverge for a competitive claim), power-law exponents log(acc_inf - acc) vs log(n).
gate.registered_prediction: the sparse ridge head is O(n*W^2) with W=12288, so at small n it is underdetermined and should sit below the dense trunk; as n grows past W the gap should close. Whether the gain ratio clears 0.5 is the open question (the family saturates at 0.2153 on the accuracy axis, but the SHAPE of Q_S(n) is independent of the absolute ceiling). Prior art: Bardone-Goldt (2603.12901) predicts linear-sample learnability of higher cumulants with shared latent structure; Ghorbani (2020) bounds random-feature accuracy, not its data-scaling shape.
